S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

patient_info.stressor_event: Changing to a different line of work
patient_info.stressor: Two years and two months ago, Lois moved from a more predictable education-adjacent role into advertising sales strategy, where rapid client calls, proposal deadlines, CRM tracking, and team pitches replaced quieter one-on-one work. Early lapses that she covered with late-night crossword-like checklists grew into repeated trouble sustaining attention through meetings, missing parts of instructions, leaving tasks unfinished, losing campaign materials, and speaking out of turn during sales discussions, while her difficulty sitting through long strategy sessions and waiting her turn began to affect her performance reviews. She sought psychiatric evaluation herself after a valued learning-focused client complained that her scattered follow-through undermined an otherwise ethical and thoughtful campaign plan.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: In longer strategy meetings or while reading a client brief, I start out focused, but after a few minutes I realize I have been staring at the same slide or paragraph and have no idea what the last point was.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: When my manager gives me feedback or a client is explaining what they want changed, I can be looking right at them and nodding, then seconds later I have to ask them to repeat the part I just missed.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: I’ll get most of a proposal or CRM update done, but then I leave off the last step, like sending the final version or logging the follow-up, even though I meant to finish it.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: My campaign notes end up split between emails, sticky notes, my planner, and random tabs, and I waste a lot of time figuring out what to do first instead of just starting.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for things I need for work, like my headset, client one-pagers, keys, or the notebook I was using ten minutes earlier.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: Honestly, what made me come in is that I keep getting up during long sales strategy meetings when I know I’m supposed to stay seated, even if it’s just to refill water or pace by the printer.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: In team pitches I can hear myself going on too long about the campaign idea, and by the time I stop, I can tell other people were waiting for a chance to speak.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: I often jump in with an answer before a client or coworker has finished asking the question, and then I realize I answered the wrong thing or cut them off.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Waiting my turn on client calls or in office discussions makes me restless, so I keep checking the clock or rehearsing what I want to say until I blurt it out too early.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: If I think of an idea while someone else is working through a deck, I’ll pop over or interrupt their conversation to add my thought, even when it probably could have waited.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I remember this starting way before high school—my elementary school teachers wrote that I was bright but rushed, talked out of turn, forgot homework, and had a desk stuffed with half-finished papers.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: At work, it has started showing up in performance reviews and client trust; one client complaint especially made me worry that I could damage accounts even though I care a lot about doing good work.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been noticeably affecting me since I changed into advertising sales strategy about two years and two months ago.
